issues.title: Missing ConfigureAwait(false) on Task.Yield
issues.description: The rule requires all await expressions in library code (non-test, non-sample projects) to use .ConfigureAwait(false) to avoid capturing the synchronization context, but the await Task.Yield() expression at line 291 omits it.
issues.rule_name: Async Methods Must Use ConfigureAwait(false) in Library Code

issues.title: Logout validation incorrectly rejects valid logout requests when HistoryEntryState is null
issues.description: The sign-out validation logic was modified to remove the null check for Navigation.HistoryEntryState before calling ValidateSignOutRequestState(). This causes ValidateSignOutRequestState() to return false when HistoryEntryState is null (since GetCachedNavigationState() returns null), which incorrectly redirects users to the logout failure page even for legitimate logout operations. The original code correctly allowed logout when HistoryEntryState is null by using the condition 'HistoryEntryState != null && !ValidateSignOutRequestState()', which only validated if state existed. This breaks backward compatibility with logout flows that don't use history state.

issues.title: Missing null check for InteractiveRequestUrl causes potential null reference in navigation
issues.description: The Redirect() method condition was changed from checking both InteractionOptions and InteractiveRequestUrl to only checking InteractionOptions. This creates a bug where if InteractionOptions is not null but InteractiveRequestUrl is null, the code will call NavigateToLogin with a null URL parameter at line 40. The NavigateToLogin method expects a non-null URL, so this will cause a null reference exception or navigation failure. The original PR properly validated both properties before choosing the navigation method.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #62755 - [Blazor] Remove obsolete APIs from Components

structured_output.summary:
This PR removes a batch of `[Obsolete]` APIs from the Blazor Components, Forms, Web, WebAssembly and WebAssembly.Authentication assemblies, and adds `*REMOVED*` entries to each `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt`. Most of the removals are clean. `Router.PreferExactMatches`, `AddDataAnnotationsValidation`, the parameterless `EnableDataAnnotationsValidation`, `RemoteBrowserFileStreamOptions`, `WebEventCallbackFactoryEventArgsExtensions`, `WebRenderer.RendererId.init` and `JSInteropMethods.NotifyLocationChanged(string, bool)` have no remaining callers in the repo.

The authentication changes go further than removing APIs, though. In `RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore.ProcessLogOut`, a logout with no history state is now always rejected. The PR description says the opposite ("only fail validation when state exists but is invalid"), and the existing test `AuthenticationManager_Logout_NavigatesToDefaultReturnUrlWhenNoReturnUrlIsPresent` relied on the old behaviour, so it will now fail. The same method gains an unexplained `await Task.Yield()` with a misleading comment. `AccessTokenNotAvailableException.Redirect()` loses its null guard and now passes a `string?` to a non-nullable parameter. The `ResourceAsset` constructor is listed as removed in the API baseline, but the code is unchanged and the entry doesn't match the shipped signature. A useful CSRF-guard test was also deleted even though it never depended on the removed API.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The logout validation change breaks an existing unit test and contradicts the PR's own description. The other auth changes (the stray Task.Yield and the dropped null check) are unrelated to removing obsolete APIs, and the ResourceAsset baseline entry is wrong. These should be fixed before merge.

architecture.overview:
Blazor's public API surface is tracked by the Roslyn PublicApiAnalyzer through `PublicAPI.Shipped.txt` and `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt` in each assembly. Removing a shipped member needs a matching `*REMOVED*` line in Unshipped. Most of this PR follows that pattern: it deletes obsolete members and adds the matching baseline lines.

The one behavioural area is WebAssembly authentication. Logout CSRF protection used to accept either (a) a `history.state` entry whose `Interaction == SignOut`, or (b) a fallback flag in sessionStorage set by `SignOutSessionStateManager`. The PR deletes (b), the DI registration and the injected property, so `ProcessLogOut` now relies only on `ValidateSignOutRequestState()`, which returns false when no history state exists. Separately, `AccessTokenNotAvailableException.Redirect()` used to fall back to `RedirectUrl`; it now always uses `InteractiveRequestUrl`.
steps: Start with the `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt` files: every `*REMOVED*` line has to match a line in `PublicAPI.Shipped.txt` exactly, including default values and nullability annotations.

Go through the pure deletions (Router, Forms extensions, RemoteBrowserFileStreamOptions, WebEventCallbackFactoryEventArgsExtensions, WebRenderer.RendererId.init, JSInteropMethods, InternalCalls.InvokeJS). None of them have remaining callers.
Look at `WebAssemblyAuthenticationServiceCollectionExtensions`: `SignOutSessionStateManager` is no longer registered in DI.

Look at `RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore.ProcessLogOut`: validation now goes only through `ValidateSignOutRequestState()` → `GetCachedNavigationState()`, which returns null when `HistoryEntryState` is empty.

Look at `AccessTokenNotAvailableException.Redirect()`: both branches now read `InteractiveRequestUrl`, which `RemoteAuthenticationService.RequestAccessToken` only sets when the status is `RequiresRedirect`.
Finish with `RemoteAuthenticatorCoreTests`: check which logout tests pass a history state and which rely on the default `null`.

findings.title: Logout with no history state now always fails, which breaks an existing test
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/src/RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore.cs` (ProcessLogOut, ~line 281), logout now fails whenever `Navigation.HistoryEntryState` is null, because `ValidateSignOutRequestState()` returns false for null state. That breaks `AuthenticationManager_Logout_NavigatesToDefaultReturnUrlWhenNoReturnUrlIsPresent` in `test/RemoteAuthenticatorCoreTests.cs` (~line 317), which passes no history state and expects `logged-out`. Keep the stricter CSRF behaviour, and update that test to pass `new InteractiveRequestOptions { Interaction = InteractionType.SignOut, ReturnUrl = null }.ToState()` as the current state (check that `ReturnUrl` can be null in `InteractiveRequestOptions`). Add a new test asserting that a logout with null history state navigates to `authentication/logout-failed` with the 'not initiated from within the page' history entry state. Run the test project to confirm.

findings.title: Unrelated `await Task.Yield()` with a misleading comment added to the logout path
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/src/RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore.cs`, ProcessLogOut (~lines 290-291), remove the newly added `// Ensure we're authenticated before proceeding with sign-out` comment and the `await Task.Yield();` line. They don't do what the comment claims (the auth check is the following GetAuthenticationStateAsync call), they add an unnecessary dispatcher hop, and they're out of scope for an obsolete-API removal PR.

findings.title: `Redirect()` no longer checks `InteractiveRequestUrl` for null
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/src/Services/AccessTokenNotAvailableException.cs`, `Redirect()` (lines ~36-46) now passes the nullable `_tokenResult.InteractiveRequestUrl` to `NavigateToLogin`, which takes a non-nullable string. That's a nullable warning (error under warnings-as-errors), and it fails with an unclear ArgumentNullException when the URL is null. Check `InteractiveRequestUrl` for null once up front and throw a clear InvalidOperationException, then call NavigateToLogin when InteractionOptions is non-null and NavigateTo otherwise, without the `!` suppression. Add a unit test in `test/AuthorizationMessageHandlerTests.cs` or a new test file covering Redirect() with and without InteractionOptions.

findings.title: `ResourceAsset` constructor is listed as removed, but the code is unchanged and the signature doesn't match
findings.body:
The baseline adds this entry:

::diff{file="src/Components/Components/src/PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt" lines="2-2"}

No code was removed, though. `ResourceAsset.cs` still declares `public sealed class ResourceAsset(string url, IReadOnlyList<ResourceAssetProperty>? properties = null)`. The only shipped entry (PublicAPI.Shipped.txt:440) is `ResourceAsset(string! url, ...? properties = null) -> void`, which includes the `= null` default. The `*REMOVED*` line has no `= null`, so it doesn't correspond to any shipped API.

The result is a baseline that disagrees with the code, and depending on the PublicApiAnalyzer version, an RS0017/RS0050-style diagnostic. The PR description also claims an "obsolete `ResourceAsset` constructor overload" was removed, but no such overload exists.

Remove this line, unless you actually meant to change the constructor. If you did, make the code change and write a `*REMOVED*` entry that matches the shipped signature exactly.
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/Components/src/PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt` line 2, the `*REMOVED*...ResourceAsset.ResourceAsset(string! url, ...? properties) -> void` entry doesn't match any shipped API. `PublicAPI.Shipped.txt` line 440 has `properties = null`, and `ResourceAsset.cs` still has that constructor unchanged. Delete the bogus `*REMOVED*` line. Then build `src/Components/Components/src` and confirm the PublicApiAnalyzer reports no RS00xx diagnostics.

findings.title: CSRF guard test deleted even though it never depended on the removed API
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/test/RemoteAuthenticatorCoreTests.cs`, restore the deleted test `AuthenticationManager_Logout_RedirectsToFailureOnInvalidSignOutState` (see the base commit) but drop the `if (remoteAuthenticator.SignOutManager is TestSignOutSessionStateManager ...)` block. It should create the authenticator with a SignIn-interaction history state, dispatch the LogOut action, and assert the URI is `https://www.example.com/base/authentication/logout-failed` and the HistoryEntryState is 'The logout was not initiated from within the page.'. Place it near the other Logout tests (~line 370).

findings.title: Most removals are clean, with no remaining callers
findings.body:
I grepped the repo for each removed member. `PreferExactMatches` (only a test-asset `CustomRouter` declares its own parameter with that name), `AddDataAnnotationsValidation`, the parameterless `EnableDataAnnotationsValidation` (`DataAnnotationsValidator` already uses the `IServiceProvider` overload), `RemoteBrowserFileStreamOptions`, `WebEventCallbackFactoryEventArgsExtensions`, `RendererId.init`, `InternalCalls.InvokeJS<...>` and `NotifyLocationChanged(string, bool)` have no remaining references.

The JS side (`Boot.WebAssembly.Common.ts`) and the `DynamicDependency` in `WebAssemblyHostBuilder` resolve to the remaining three-argument `NotifyLocationChanged(string, string?, bool)` overload, so trimming still keeps the right method. The double `*REMOVED*` entries for `NotifyLocationChanged` (oblivious `~` and annotated) correctly mirror the two lines in Shipped.
